taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 405, Hookera coronaria: "scapes stout, 2-5 dm. high".

traits.perennation.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 405, Hookera coronaria: "Corm sub-globose, 18-25 mm. broad".

traits.inflorescence.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 405, Hookera coronaria: "umbels open, 2-11- flowered".

traits.flower_size_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 405, Hookera coronaria: "perianth violet-purple, 25-40 mm. long; the tube funnel-form, about half the length of the narrowly oblong, thick and persistent, segments".

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 405, Hookera coronaria: "Leaves usually about equalling the scape. 2 mm. wide, thick or somewhat terete".

appearance.organs.flower.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 405, Hookera coronaria: an open umbel of 2 to 11 violet-purple flowers on stout, unequal pedicels (the scan reads "3S cm. long", taken as 3-8 cm), each a funnel-form tube about half as long as its six segments, with white staminodia. Drawn as 6 flowers about 3.5 cm long on pedicels of about 5 cm, the tube a third of each tepal.

generator.params.note: Camas's values, changed by hand for harvest brodiaea: one stout scape from a corm ending in an open umbel, with three narrow, thick leaves about as long as the scape (Abrams 1923 p. 405). Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 0.35 m tall at 4 years in the open, the middle of Abrams's 2-5 dm scapes. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: By eye, after Abrams (1923 p. 405): violet-purple flowers with white staminodia; green scape and leaves; a straw-brown capsule.
